name: St. Paul's Church, Clinton and Mather streets

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: Established 1868 and destroyed by the fire (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406).

change_note: Built T-3831 (2026-11-28): the church in place of the generic brick block the context city stood on its lot.

placement.position_note: On the north-east corner of Clinton and Mather streets (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 406, 716-718), its front on the east walk of Clinton Street and its south side on the line of Mather Street, which the 1871 plan does not draw east of Clinton. The footprint's origin is local E -246.2 N -1531.0; the frame is turned onto the 1871 plan's grid.
placement.symbolic_location: North-east corner of Clinton and Mather streets.

footprint.note: A hundred feet by forty (Sheahan and Upton, the Catholic losses); laid with its length along Mather Street, reconstructed.

blocks.name: the church
blocks.note: A frame church a hundred feet by forty (Sheahan and Upton's list of the Catholic losses), 'of wood' (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 717-718), its front on Clinton Street and its length along Mather; the 'high church' of the Board's report (Andreas p. 716). No picture of it is known: its storeys, its pointed lights, door and roof are reconstructed as a plain frame church of its $15,000 cost (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406).

towers.name: the cupola
towers.note: Riley saw the brand fall 'on the cupola' (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 715-716): the church had one. Its place over the front, its stages, louvred belfry and bell-shaped cap are reconstructed.

value.note: ST. PAUL'S CHURCH, built by T-3831: the church whose cupola took the brand that carried the fire north.

fire.note: 'In flames while the main fire was yet four blocks away' (Andreas p. 716), and down by ten (p. 718).

composition.note: No picture of St. Paul's is known: the church is built from the accounts' words (wood, a cupola, 100 by 40 feet, $15,000) in the archetype's frame vocabulary.

wall_material.value: Painted weatherboards on a frame, a shingle roof
wall_material.note: 'Of wood' (Andreas p. 718); the paint and shingles are reconstructed.

function.note: St. Paul's Catholic church, established 1868 by members from St. Francis of Assisi; Rev. John Kilkenny pastor 1870-71 (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406).

built.note: Established in 1868 at the corner of Mather and Clinton streets (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406); the church-edifice is taken to date from then.

citations.citation: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 2, From 1857 until the Fire of 1871. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885.
what_it_supplies: clock hours at named places along the fire's path, 8-9 October 1871
the south line of the South Division ruin (Harrison and Congress streets) and where the fire was stopped
that M. D. Ogden's house on the North Side escaped
the gale from the south-west and the rain about eleven o'clock Monday night
what_it_does_not_supply: a surveyed outline of the burnt district
an hour for most individual buildings, which are interpolated between its stated hours

citations.citation: Sheahan, James W., and George P. Upton. The Great Conflagration. Chicago: Its Past, Present and Future. Philadelphia: Union Publishing Co., 1871.
what_it_supplies: the authors' count of the people made homeless by the fire of October 1871: 98,860
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about the buildings of 1812 or 1835: the town those scenes show was gone long before 1871

research_note: ST. PAUL'S CHURCH, built by T-3831 for the 1871 scene: the wooden Catholic church on the north-east corner of Clinton and Mather streets, a hundred feet by forty, that cost $15,000 (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406; Sheahan and Upton). A brand from the O'Leary fire, 'whirling through the air for more than three blocks', lit its cupola (Richard Riley, Andreas pp. 715-716); 'At ten o'clock ... the church had gone down in ruins in advance of the main body of flame' (p. 718). No picture of it is known.
